deal_summary: The customer pursued a labeling solution with a real-sample validation requirement; discussion advanced into contract and invoice processing after the seller disclosed a long build time and deferred testing until manufacture (evidence 0, 1, 2, 3, 4).

customer_need.summary: The manager log describes automating hand-applied labeling; the customer asked about 1,000 units per hour, lead time, and testing the proposed setup on its own container and label (evidence 0, 1).

deal_dynamics.early: The seller shared a quote and a comparable-project video; the customer checked speed, lead time, label handling, and whether the displayed solution was a real prototype (evidence 0, 1).
deal_dynamics.middle: The customer wanted a test on its own packaging, but the seller said no unit was available and testing would follow manufacture; production quoted up to 55 working days (evidence 1, 2).
deal_dynamics.late: The parties reviewed contract changes and the customer asked whether 70% of a 954,000 invoice was the agreed first payment; a worklog says documents were signed and a payment order sent, but no bank confirmation appears (evidence 3, 4, 5).

positive_signals: The customer asked detailed performance and label-sensing questions and supplied an equipment questionnaire (evidence 0, 1).
The customer proceeded to contract and asked for confirmation of the 70% payment split (evidence 3, 4).
negative_signals: The customer sought a real sample test before purchase, which could not be performed on an available unit (evidence 1).
customer_behavior.initiative: The customer asked for a prototype/test, queried the lead time, and returned contract corrections (evidence 0, 1, 3).
customer_behavior.decision_process: The customer evaluated technical fit and then used e-signature and staged payment steps; payment completion is not directly evidenced (evidence 1, 4, 5).

strong_actions: The seller gave direct answers about the prototype and manufacturing lead time (evidence 1, 2).
The seller processed customer contract corrections and clarified the staged invoice amount (evidence 3, 4).
weak_actions: The proposed proof of fit was deferred until after manufacture, leaving the customer's sample-validation concern unresolved before contracting (evidence 1, 2).
manager_behavior.follow_up_quality: The seller stayed engaged through technical, contract, and payment questions (evidence 1, 3, 4).
manager_behavior.next_step_control: The visible next step was the customer's 70% invoice payment and production start, but receipt is not independently confirmed (evidence 4, 5).

turning_points.description: The customer asked to test the proposal on its own container and label (evidence 0).
The seller clarified that a real test would occur only after manufacture and gave a lead time of up to 55 working days (evidence 1, 2).
The customer asked to confirm the 70% first payment on the invoice (evidence 4).

primary_trajectory_explanation.category: sample-validation requirement followed by contract processing
primary_trajectory_explanation.explanation: The main decision tension was the customer's need to validate application on its own packaging against the seller's lack of a ready unit and a 55-working-day build period. The process then advanced to contract/invoice steps, though payment and production release remain unverified here (evidence 0, 1, 2, 4, 5).

secondary_factors: The customer returned one contract correction, which was routed for review (evidence 3).
The agreed 70/30 payment split reduced the amount due at order stage but is not proof of receipt (evidence 4, 5).

what_could_be_done: Agree an explicit sample-validation protocol and acceptance criteria before promising the production schedule (evidence 0, 1, 2).
Track contract signature and payment receipt separately from a sent payment order (evidence 4, 5).
limits: No finished unit was available for a pre-purchase trial (evidence 1).
The customer controls its payment and signature timing (evidence 4, 5).

uncertainties: The initial requirement is partly from a manager worklog (evidence 0).
A manager worklog says the e-signed contract and payment order were sent, while customer messages only confirm the payment split discussion; no bank receipt is shown (evidence 4, 5).
The view ends before the requested customer-specific test or commissioning result (evidence 1, 2).

evidence.paraphrase: Manager log describes the customer as seeking automation of hand labeling and records a target price range and packaging.
Customer asks whether the image is a real prototype and whether the seller can test on the customer's jar and label.
Seller says the shown equipment is from an earlier project, none is currently available for testing, and testing will occur after manufacture.
Customer returns contract corrections involving signatures and supply-document wording.
Customer asks whether 70% of the 954,000 invoice is the correct first payment.
Manager worklog says the contract was signed through e-signature and the payment order was sent; this is a worklog claim, not bank confirmation.
